messages.text: Hi, my daughter is doing her GCSEs this year. Can she get extra time in her exams if she has dyslexia?

Yes, that's called an Access Arrangement. If she has a diagnosed learning difficulty like dyslexia, her school's SENCO can apply for up to 50% extra time. This needs to be approved by JCQ before the exam series.
Does the school need any evidence for that?

Yes, they'll need an up-to-date assessment report, usually from an educational psychologist, showing a substantial and long-term difficulty. The school keeps this on file - they don't need to send it to us unless we ask.
Great, and if she's not happy with a grade, can she ask for a re-mark?
Yes, that's a Review of Marking. Schools have to submit priority reviews within a few days of results day if she wants it back before university offers are confirmed, so I'd get that request in fast.
No problem, glad I could help. Is there anything else I can do for you today?
